Subject: Residency chain-of-custody and PrivateLink validation request

Chloe / Redwood team,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call yesterday. As part of Medicore's procurement security gate we need two items to proceed:

1) A short chain-of-custody statement that explains where customer data resides (EU), how transfers are controlled, and the last-mile PrivateLink/privatelink-equivalent topology for EU-hosted workloads.
2) Confirmation that operator access to HSM/KMS is partitioned and that operator credentials for EU nodes are distinct from US/APAC operators (we'll accept a roster + statement).

Can you provide a PDF manifest and the PrivateLink diagram by EOD Wednesday? We will attach to the SIG questionnaire and follow up with any clarifying questions.

Appreciate it — Sam
Medicore Procurement

Chloe / Marissa — copied the tech details below to paste into the SIG reply.

Operator & KMS partitioning (summary):
- EU production nodes are in a regional tenant isolated at the network and control-plane level. Crypto keys used for EU tenant encryption are created in a dedicated EU KMS key ring (HSM-backed where required).
- Operator roles are scoped per-region. EU operator accounts are bound to an EU operator group with JIT access via our privileged access workflow; global operator credentials are not authorized for EU production clusters.
- Access proof: attached operator_roster_v1.csv (redacted), and a short attestation paragraph below that legal can include verbatim.

Attestation paragraph (suggested):
"Redwood Inference confirms that customer data for EU-hosted tenants is processed and stored on EU-resident infrastructure. Access to EU production nodes is restricted to EU-scoped operators via a region-scoped privileged access group. KMS keys for EU tenants are created and stored within an EU HSM-backed key ring; no global operator credentials have administrative access to EU HSM key material."

Attachments included: [operator_roster_v1.csv (redacted)] and a link to the internal topology diagram (privatelink_topology.png).
